title: Replace watchdog+launchd-respawn RTSP reconnect with single-thread in-thread periodic teardown (Frigate/go2rtc pattern)
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-16, post the hourly-restart diagnostic)
trigger: Operator 2026-09-16 (verbatim): 'It doesn't need a watchdog, it doesn't need to restart the listener, it just needs to tear down the RTSP stream and start a new one every hour. The watchdog and the listener restart are both problems that should not be in the code, they are lazy workarounds.' And: 'It is horrible design, and it is actually embarrassing.' Confirmed by 11-hour overnight audit: decoder threads wedge silently in libav C demux() (PyAV issue #700), the watchdog's 'completed (reconnects_total=1)' log is decorative (decode threads do not exit within 10s on every fire, six per daemon), and launchd KeepAlive=true then kills+restarts the entire listener 600ms later. The internal watchdog is a paper trail; launchd is the actual reconnect mechanism. Industry-canonical pattern (Frigate, go2rtc producer.go) owns the connect/decode/disconnect cycle on the single thread that consumes the frames -- no watchdog thread, no outer process restart. V1 design contract per operator 2026-09-16: tear down + reopen every hour from inside the decode loop.
background: Current state in /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2/infra/frame_capture.py: PersistentRTSPReader.start() spawns TWO threads per camera: a decode thread (target=self._run_loop) AND a watchdog thread (target=self._scheduled_reconnect_watchdog). The watchdog sleeps on stop_event with timeout=scheduled_reconnect_seconds (default 3600), then calls _scheduled_reconnect_fire() which: (a) sets stop_event so the decode thread exits on next packet, (b) joins the decode thread with a 10s timeout, (c) closes the container, (d) spawns a NEW decode thread. In practice (overnight audit 2026-09-15 21:00 to 2026-09-16 08:00, logs/daemon.log): every fire logs 'decode thread did not exit within 10s' for ALL SIX cameras simultaneously, then 'scheduled_reconnect_fire: completed (reconnects_total=1)' -- the new decode threads spawn ALONGSIDE the wedged ones. launchctl then restarts the daemon 600ms later because the listener stops emitting output. Net effect: the watchdog is decorative, the hourly cadence is provided by launchd KeepAlive=true, and the system survives only because the daemon respawn is fast enough to not lose frames the alert pipeline cares about. V1 design knew the RTSP stream becomes unstable at ~6h. The fix is a periodic teardown from the thread that owns the libav context, not a layer of paper that the operator must trust blindly. Web research confirms go2rtc internal/streams/producer.go uses a single producer() goroutine with internal reconnect() method (no watchdog, no outer process), Frigate uses the same pattern, and PyAV #700 explicitly says demux() can wedge silently and must be torn down by the application. Phase 6B.13 / Phase 6B.39 baked in the bad design (defensive 'proceed anyway' branch that the V1 refactor never had); this PRD supersedes both.
goal: PersistentRTSPReader owns its own lifecycle: a single decode thread that runs the decode loop, AND from inside the same loop tears down + reopens the libav container on a fixed cadence (every 3600s by default). No watchdog thread. No launchd KeepAlive. No defense layers. Daemon crashes fail loud; healthy hours progress silently.

design_principles: One thread per camera. The decode thread owns the libav container for its lifetime.
Periodic teardown happens INSIDE _decode_iteration -- NOT in a sibling thread.
Every reconnect (scheduled OR failure-driven) re-opens the container by re-entering _decode_iteration. The outer while loop in _run_loop is the single entry point.
Ring buffer survives ALL reconnects (scheduled teardown, failure-driven reconnect, cap-exhausted retry). PersistentRTSPReader._ring is owned by the PersistentRTSPReader.
Failure-driven reconnect stays capped at RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS_DEFAULT (10). After cap, log ERROR and exit the decode loop with healthy=False. is_healthy() returns False. No fallback path.
Tests live next to code. test_rtsp_watchdog.py is removed; its cases migrate to test_frame_capture.py under clearer names.

AC5: cd /Users/jill/farm-surveillance-v2 && python -m pytest tests/test_frame_capture.py -q --no-header 2>&1 | tail -3 (existing failure-driven reconnect tests still pass -- cap logic in _run_loop is unchanged)
stories.notes: Pattern (model after go2rtc producer.go reconnect()): _decode_iteration loops on container.demux(stream). Between packet iterations, check (time.monotonic() - self._last_teardown_monotonic) >= TEARDOWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (3600.0). On trigger: close container in a try/except that re-raises on real errors (no `except: pass`), reopen via av.open in this same frame, update self._last_teardown_monotonic, continue. self._ring is class-level -- persists across teardown by construction. stats() must expose last_teardown_monotonic and seconds_since_teardown.
stories.story_size_budget: rewrite of _decode_iteration, ~40 net new lines, fits in one commit
